memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Moses set up the tabernacle, he put the bases in place, erected the frames, inserted the crossbars and set up the posts. Then he spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering over the tent, as the Lord commanded him." - Exod 40:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Bases first. Then frames. Then crossbars. Then posts. Then the tent, then the covering.

It came together in order, one stage at a time. You cannot raise frames before the bases are set, and you cannot spread the covering before the frames stand.

Most of what God builds in us works this way. Not all at once — in sequence, with each stage resting on the one before.

That is worth remembering when growth feels slow. Someone praying for patience may find God working first on humility, because patience without humility is only self-control with pride underneath. We often want the covering when God is still setting bases.

Paul described his own experience as pressing on toward what is ahead, not having already obtained it (Phil 3:12-14). And he was confident that God, who began the work, would carry it on to completion (Phil 1:6).

Notice too that Moses did the assembling himself. After all the craftsmen's work, the leader set it up piece by piece.

There is dignity in patient, sequential work. Not everything in the Christian life is a breakthrough. Much of it is putting the next piece in place, today, in order.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you frustrated that God is not working faster in some area?
2. What foundation might God be laying before the thing you are asking for?
3. What is the next single piece you need to put in place?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I want the finished thing, and You are building in order. Give me patience for the next piece. Amen.
